summary: John's 4th-great-grandfather; Plymouth farmer, son of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreaux) Pringle, who married into the Palatine German Croup family.
bio: James Pringle was born about 1799 in Pennsylvania (1850 census: 51, farmer, real estate $500, b. PA); the tree shows 1798-?, and a FamilySearch profile's '1799-1909' death is impossible (probably a merge). He was a son of Samuel Pringle and Martha Lamoreaux (Harvey Book pp.370-371, via his son Noah). He married Elizabeth Croup, daughter of Frederick Croup and Mary Young of Hunlock's Creek/Nanticoke. In 1850 the household in Plymouth Twp (dwelling 944/family 964, 14 Sep 1850) was James 51, Elizabeth 48, Alby 27, Noah 16, Andrew 14, Leva Ann 11 and Edwin 9; neighbours were Jenkins Jones (36, miner, Wales; dwelling 943) and Thomas Gould (39, farmer, $2,500; dwelling 945), with his probable sister-in-law the widow Hulda Pringle at dwelling 942. FamilySearch gives a second wife, Mary Steele (d. 15 Jul 1876), and burial in Scott Cemetery, Huntington Mills. He is not the runaway apprentice 'James Pringle', about 14, advertised by Isaac Smith of Exeter Twp on 9 Apr 1836, nor his uncle James Pringle who married Phebe Lamoreux in 1785.
